items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are cryptic throughout and the whole query sits on one line: CTEs `a`, `t`, `c`, alias `y`, columns `ts`, `tn`, `dd`, `dp`, `n`. Many CTEs and subqueries are packed into a single line with no indentation, unlike the readable named-CTE style the project asks for.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The structure is sound: aggregate once, take the top 500, then ROW_NUMBER for the top synset, with no copy-pasted correlated subqueries. But the one-line layout and opaque aliases make it hard to change. The `LEFT JOIN c` is unnecessary because tn>=2 guarantees a match.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: This is a read-only query. It adds no new magic constants (the thresholds 2 and the limit 500 come from the original), and the LEFT JOIN cannot drop rows. There are no error-handling concerns.

items.name: Semantically equivalent, not just equal on this data
items.name_zh: 语义等价而非仅在当前数据上相等
items.evidence: It keeps the HAVING thresholds, COUNT(DISTINCT), the (n DESC, synsetid ASC) tie-break, the ORDER BY with the wordid tie-break, and LIMIT 500. But it groups by senses.wordid and joins `words` only after aggregating, so it assumes wordid is unique in `words`, which the schema has no PK to guarantee. Duplicate rows would give different results.
